title: When all desires are let go
theme: When all the desires that lodge in one’s heart are let go, then the mortal becomes immortal; here he attains Brahman.

sandhi.rule: After ā the visarga becomes y before a voiced sound, P. 8.3.17 (भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि), and the y is dropped before a consonant, P. 8.3.22 (हलि सर्वेषाम्).
After e at the end of a word an initial a is merged into it, P. 6.1.109 (एङः पदान्तादति); the avagraha marks it.

sandhi.type: aḥ before a; aḥ before a voiced consonant; i before an unlike vowel
sandhi.rule: The visarga of -aḥ becomes u before a, giving o, P. 6.1.114 (हशि च) with P. 6.1.87 (आद्गुणः), and the following a is merged, P. 6.1.109 (एङः पदान्तादति); the avagraha marks it. -aḥ becomes -o before a voiced consonant, P. 6.1.114 (हशि च). i before an unlike vowel becomes y, P. 6.1.77 (इको यणचि).

morphology.note: Passive present of pra + √muc, ‘are released, fall away’: the desires are let go, not the person.
sam + √aś (5th class), ‘reach, attain fully’, in the middle voice.

translation.literal: When all [the] desires which lodge in his heart are released, then the mortal becomes immortal; here [he] attains Brahman.
translation.readable: When all the desires that dwell in the heart fall away, then the mortal becomes immortal, and attains Brahman here and now.

syntax: A temporal clause (yadā sarve pramucyante kāmāḥ) with a relative clause on kāmāḥ (ye ’sya hṛdi śritāḥ), answered by atha with two main clauses: martyo ’mṛto bhavati and atra brahma samaśnute.

ambiguities.topic: ‘Here’: in this life, or in meditation?
ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara: here, in this very life, all bonds ceasing as a lamp goes out, he becomes Brahman, «अत्र इहैव प्रदीपनिर्वाणवत्सर्वबन्धनोपशमात् ब्रह्म समश्नुते ब्रह्मैव भवतीत्यर्थः». Raṅgarāmānuja: here, at the time of meditation, he experiences Brahman, «अत्रैव उपासनवेलायां ब्रह्मानुभवति इत्यर्थः».

Śaṅkara: death, which is ignorance, desire and action, is destroyed, so there is no more going, «गमनप्रयोजकस्य मृत्योर्विनाशाद्गमनानुपपत्तेः». Raṅgarāmānuja: past sins are destroyed and later ones do not cling, «विश्लिष्टाश्लिष्ट पूर्वोत्तरदुरितभरो भवति इत्यर्थः», following the Brahmasūtra and the Bhāṣya he quotes.

beginner: This verse names what has to end for the self to be found: the desires that live in the heart. When all of them fall away, it says, the mortal becomes immortal and reaches Brahman right here. The Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad has the same verse word for word. Śaṅkara explains that desires belong to the mind, not to the self, and that when one knows the self there is nothing left to want. Then death, which for him means ignorance, desire and action, comes to an end, and one becomes Brahman in this very life, as a lamp goes out. Raṅgarāmānuja reads ‘immortal’ as being freed from the weight of past wrongdoing, with later wrongs no longer clinging, and ‘here’ as the time of meditation, when the meditator already experiences Brahman. Madhva’s comment, in verse, says that one freed from desire will not go towards death.
analogy: A boat tied to the shore by many ropes floats free only when the last rope is untied.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: When all desires lodged in the heart are let go, the mortal becomes immortal and attains Brahman here.

commentary.q: Śaṅkara: desires belong to the intellect, not to the self
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: For one who sees the highest self, desires fall away because there is nothing else to desire, «कामयितव्यस्यान्यस्याभावात्». They rest in the intellect, not the self, «बुद्धिर्हि कामानामाश्रयः नात्मा», as another scripture says, ‘desire, resolve…’ (quoted by him). Death, which is ignorance, desire and action, is destroyed, and with it all going; here, as a lamp goes out, he becomes Brahman, «अत्र इहैव प्रदीपनिर्वाणवत्सर्वबन्धनोपशमात् ब्रह्म समश्नुते ब्रह्मैव भवतीत्यर्थः».

commentary.q: Raṅgarāmānuja: freed from sin, enjoying Brahman in meditation
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: When the heart’s longings for wrong objects are stilled, the meditator becomes immortal: past sins are destroyed and later ones do not cling, «विश्लिष्टाश्लिष्ट पूर्वोत्तरदुरितभरो भवति इत्यर्थः». ‘Here’ is the time of meditation, «अत्रैव उपासनवेलायां ब्रह्मानुभवति इत्यर्थः». He quotes the Bhāṣya on the sūtra «समाना चाऽऽसृत्युपक्रमादमृतत्त्वं च अनुपोष्य» to the same effect.

commentary.q: Madhva: the freed one will not go to death
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: In a verse in his comment: when the desires of the inner organ are given up, the one freed will not go to death, «कामानां तु तदा मुक्तो मृतिं नैवाभियास्यति». His text reads hṛdi sthitāḥ and atha brahma (corrections.json).

commentary.q: The same verse in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka
commentary.label: comparative
commentary.text: The verse stands word for word in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka, «यदा सर्वे प्रमुच्यन्ते कामा येऽस्य हृदि श्रिताः».

advaita.text: With desire gone, the knower becomes Brahman in this life, «ब्रह्मैव भवतीत्यर्थः», and there is no further going.

visistadvaita.text: Immortality here is freedom from the clinging of sin; Brahman is experienced in meditation, «अत्रैव उपासनवेलायां ब्रह्मानुभवति इत्यर्थः».

dvaita.text: One freed from the desires of the inner organ does not go to death, «कामानां तु तदा मुक्तो मृतिं नैवाभियास्यति».

schools.disagreement: Śaṅkara reads ‘attains Brahman here’ as becoming Brahman in this life; Raṅgarāmānuja as experiencing Brahman in meditation while still embodied, release itself coming later; Madhva’s verse speaks of freedom from death without discussing ‘here’.

parallels.quote: यदा सर्वे प्रमुच्यन्ते कामा येऽस्य हृदि श्रिताः
parallels.note: The same verse in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka.
Quoted by Śaṅkara: desire belongs to the mind.
The sūtra under which Raṅgarāmānuja quotes the Bhāṣya on this verse.

contemporary.text: Desire usually feels like something we have to satisfy. The verse treats it as something that can be let go, and places freedom in that letting go rather than in having. This is a reflection, not a claim made by the text.

reflect.beginner: Which of your wishes would you be glad to be free of?
reflect.deeper: Is ‘here’ this life, or the hour of meditation? What would each reading ask of a reader?
reflect.practice: Notice one desire today and watch it pass without acting on it.

flags.note: Madhva’s text reads hṛdi sthitāḥ for hṛdi śritāḥ and atha brahma for atra brahma (corrections.json).
‘Here he attains Brahman’: becoming Brahman in this life (Śaṅkara) or experiencing Brahman in meditation (Raṅgarāmānuja).
